[Tea basics](tea-basics.qmd) told you what the words on the box usually mean. This page is the **kitchen complaint sheet**: bitter, flat, cloudy, or a second steep that feels different → which dial to nudge first.

It is not a second brewing textbook. The full extraction story lives in [Chapter 1 · Section 3 — What brewing actually does](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd). Typical milligrams live on the [Cup reference](cup-reference.qmd). Use **this** page when the mug already happened and you want a short “what to try next.”

Keep the [Glossary](glossary.qmd) for chapter jargon. Keep Basics for grocery and cafe labels. Keep Cup reference when “weak” really means “compare my mug to the baseline.”

::: {.callout-tip title="5-minute fix path"}
1. **Name the symptom** — bitter / flat / cloudy / second steep feels different.
2. **Turn one dial** — time, temperature, leaf amount, or leaf style (broken vs whole).
3. **Want the why?** Open [Chapter 1 · Section 3](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd).
4. **Want milligrams?** Open the [Cup reference](cup-reference.qmd).

The rest of this page is optional depth for when one nudge is not enough.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Words to know on this page"}
- **Three dials** — **time**, **temperature**, and **leaf amount** (how much leaf per mug). Chapter 1 owns the full story; this page only routes complaints to those dials.
- **Leaf style** — broken bag grades vs whole leaf change how fast compounds leave (surface area / “exit speed”), not which plant you bought.
- **Second steep** — with whole leaf, early guests leave first; later steeps often feel different. Bag grades compress that drama into one fast act.
:::

## Symptom → dial map

Start here. One compact routing sheet—kitchen language only. No new numbers; the *why* sits one click away.

| If the cup feels… | First dial to try | Then open… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bitter / harsh** | Shorter time and/or cooler water (especially greens); treat bitterness as your brake | [Chapter 1 · Section 3](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd) (heat and time also pull bitter material; [EGCG](glossary.qmd#egcg) wants more heat) |
| **Flat / pale / weak** | Longer time, hotter water (style-aware), or more leaf | [Chapter 1 · Section 3](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd) dials; [Cup reference](cup-reference.qmd) when you want a home baseline strength map |
| **Cloudy / muddy look** | Often fine particles / bag grade plus a short hot dunk—not a new plant | [Tea basics · Bag vs loose / CTC](tea-basics.qmd); Chapter 1 · Section 3 foldout on particle size / surface area |
| **Second steep different** | Expected with whole leaf: early guests leave first; bag grades compress the drama | [Chapter 1 · Section 3 — A second cup…](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd) |

**This page owns** the complaint → dial routing sheet. **It does not own** extraction kinetics, solubility tables, or lab-vs-home strength tables—those stay in Chapter 1 · Section 3 and Cup reference.

Optional hallway when “why does heat change what I feel later?” is the real question: [Linkages · bridge 3 — How brew heat reshapes the cup you feel](linkages.qmd).

## One dial at a time

Chapter 1 already taught the three home dials. Here is only a pointer habit—**change one thing**, taste again, then decide whether you need the full lesson.

- **Time** — longer usually means more compounds in the water, until taste turns too bitter for you. Early guests (caffeine and [L-theanine](glossary.qmd#l-theanine) in the Chapter 1 story) leave relatively easily; bitterness and slower guests often show up later.
- **Temperature** — hotter water pulls more overall strength and helps heat-hungry guests such as EGCG; it can also pull harshness. Style matters: greens often prefer cooler water than blacks—details in Chapter 1 · Section 3.
- **Leaf amount** — more grams per mug raises everything. When “weak” means “compare to a typical mug,” open Cup reference rather than guessing.
- **Leaf style** — broken bag grades expose more surface area, so color and strength often appear quickly; whole leaf is slower and often leaves more for a second steep. Product framing (bag vs loose, CTC vs orthodox) already sits on [Tea basics](tea-basics.qmd); the geometry story sits in Chapter 1 · Section 3.

→ Full dial story and foldouts: [Chapter 1 · Section 3 — What brewing actually does](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd)  
→ Why numbers move with temp and leaf amount: [Cup reference · Practical notes](cup-reference.qmd)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More detail: why we refuse a second brew textbook here"}
If this page rebuilt Chapter 1’s dial table, weekday kettle protocol, and solubility foldouts, you would have two brewing lessons fighting for the same job. The companion rule is simple: **one full-depth room per job**. Kitchen troubleshoot routes; Chapter 1 teaches; Cup reference maps milligrams.
:::

## Cold brew and other myths (thin)

Cold water **slows** extraction. It does **not** delete caffeine. Smile politely at “caffeine-free cold brew,” then open the myth check in Chapter 1 · Section 3—and the clock notes already on that page. When someone asks “how much caffeine then?,” compare to the [Cup reference](cup-reference.qmd) after you know how you brewed, not before.

→ [Chapter 1 · Section 3 — Myth check: Cold brew means no caffeine](modules/module-01/03-brewing.qmd)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="More detail: what this thin block refuses to invent"}
No new cold-brew recipes, no new hour counts, and no new milligram claims live on this door. If Chapter 1 or Cup reference already state a figure, follow the link. If they do not, this page stays silent rather than inventing kitchen folklore.
:::
